facts.raw_span: A 30-year-old man
asymptomatic, calcified mass on the right anterior maxilla
had been present for 18 months
mucosal fenestration through which a hard, mineralized structure approximately 1 cm in diameter was visible
periapical radiograph of the upper right premolar area demonstrated a discrete radiopaque lesion
initial diagnostic hypothesis was maxillary exostosis
incisional biopsy was performed to remove a fragment of the lesion
submitted for histopathological analysis

concepts.why: The presence of a calcified mass on the right anterior maxilla and a discrete radiopaque lesion on the periapical radiograph supports this diagnosis.
The location and characteristics of the mass are consistent with a periosteal osteoma.
The presence of a hard, mineralized structure and a discrete radiopaque lesion could be indicative of a compound odontoma.
The clinical and radiographic features are consistent with a fibro-osseous lesion.
The location and characteristics of the mass could be indicative of a torus palatinus.
The presence of a calcified mass and a discrete radiopaque lesion could be indicative of an osteochondroma.

rationales.F02: The presence of an asymptomatic, calcified mass on the right anterior maxilla suggests a possible bony lesion, which is consistent with maxillary exostosis and periosteal osteoma.
rationales.F04: The mucosal fenestration with a hard, mineralized structure visible is consistent with a bony lesion such as maxillary exostosis or periosteal osteoma.
rationales.F05: The discrete radiopaque lesion on the periapical radiograph is consistent with a bony lesion such as maxillary exostosis or periosteal osteoma.
rationales.F06: The initial diagnostic hypothesis of maxillary exostosis provides strong evidence for this condition.
